q: A plant disease is usually defined as abnormal ____ and/or dysfunction of a plant.
e: A plant disease is usually defined as abnormal growth and/or dysfunction of a plant. That missing piece is growth.

q: Diseases are the result of some disturbance in the normal ____ process of the plant.
e: Diseases are the result of some disturbance in the normal life process of the plant. Write life in the gap.

q: Diseases may be the result of living and/or ____ causes.
e: Diseases may be the result of living and/or non-living causes. That missing piece is non-living.

q: Biotic diseases are caused by ____ organisms (e.g., fungi, bacteria, and viruses).
e: Biotic diseases are caused by living organisms (e.g., fungi, bacteria, and viruses). The blank is living.

q: Abiotic diseases are caused by non-living ____ conditions (e.g., soil compaction, wind, frost, soil salt damage, and girdling roots).
e: Abiotic diseases are caused by non-living environmental conditions (e.g., soil compaction, wind, frost, soil salt damage, and girdling roots). The blank is environmental.

q: Plant disease is any abnormal condition that alters the appearance or ____ of a plant.
e: Plant disease is any abnormal condition that alters the appearance or function of a plant. Write function in the gap.

q: Most plant diseases, around ____ percent are caused by fungal or fungal-like organisms.
e: Most plant diseases, around 85 percent are caused by fungal or fungal-like organisms. That missing piece is 85.

q: Certain ____ also cause plant diseases.
e: Certain nematodes also cause plant diseases. The blank is nematodes.

q: Nematodes are very tiny ____.
e: Nematodes are very tiny roundworms. Write roundworms in the gap.

q: Some plant diseases are classified as "____," or diseases that are non-infectious and include damage from air pollution, nutritional deficiencies or toxicities.
e: Some plant diseases are classified as "abiotic," or diseases that are non-infectious and include damage from air pollution, nutritional deficiencies or toxicities. Write abiotic in the gap.

q: Infectious plant diseases are caused by a ____ organism such as a fungus, bacterium, mycoplasma, virus, viroid, nematode, or parasitic flowering plant.
e: Infectious plant diseases are caused by a pathogenic organism such as a fungus, bacterium, mycoplasma, virus, viroid, nematode, or parasitic flowering plant. Write pathogenic in the gap.

q: An infectious agent is capable of ____ within or on its host and spreading from one susceptible host to another.
e: An infectious agent is capable of reproducing within or on its host and spreading from one susceptible host to another. Write reproducing in the gap.

q: Non-infectious plant diseases are caused by ____ growing conditions, including extremes of temperature.
e: Non-infectious plant diseases are caused by unfavourable growing conditions, including extremes of temperature. Write unfavourable in the gap.

q: Because non-infectious causal agents are not organisms capable of reproducing within a host, they are not ____.
e: Because non-infectious causal agents are not organisms capable of reproducing within a host, they are not transmissible. That missing piece is transmissible.

q: The study of plant diseases is called plant ____.
e: The study of plant diseases is called plant pathology. The blank is pathology.

q: Pathology is derived from the two Greek words pathos (suffering, disease) and ____ (discourse, study).
e: Pathology is derived from the two Greek words pathos (suffering, disease) and logos (discourse, study). Write logos in the gap.

q: Plant pathology thus means a study of plant ____.
e: Plant pathology so means a study of plant diseases. Write diseases in the gap.

q: Plant disease is caused by a pathogen (biotic or infectious disease) or an ____ factor (abiotic or non-infectious disease).
e: Plant disease is caused by a pathogen (biotic or infectious disease) or an environmental factor (abiotic or non-infectious disease). The blank is environmental.

q: Biotic diseases can spread throughout one plant and also may spread to ____ plants of the same species.
e: Biotic diseases can spread throughout one plant and also may spread to neighbouring plants of the same species. That missing piece is neighbouring.

q: Biotic diseases sometimes show physical evidence (signs) of the pathogen, such as fungal growth, bacterial ____, or nematode cysts.
e: Biotic diseases sometimes show physical evidence (signs) of the pathogen, such as fungal growth, bacterial ooze, or nematode cysts. That missing piece is ooze.

q: Many plant problems, especially biotic problems, if not recognized and controlled early in their development, they can result in significant ____ damage for the producer.
e: Many plant problems, especially biotic problems, if not recognized and controlled early in their development, they can result in significant economic damage for the producer. That missing piece is economic.

q: Abiotic diseases are caused by nonliving factors, such as drought stress, sunscald, freeze injury, wind injury, chemical injury, nutrient ____, or improper cultural practices.
e: Abiotic diseases are caused by nonliving factors, such as drought stress, sunscald, freeze injury, wind injury, chemical injury, nutrient deficiency, or improper cultural practices. That missing piece is deficiency.

q: Abiotic damage often occurs on many plant ____.
e: Abiotic damage often occurs on many plant species. Write species in the gap.

q: In contrast, biotic disease problems are more limited to a certain ____.
e: In contrast, biotic disease problems are more limited to a certain species. The blank is species.

q: For example, the fungi that cause tomato leaf blight do not cause damage on sweet ____.
e: The fungi that cause tomato leaf blight do not cause damage on sweet corn. That missing piece is corn.

q: Abiotic damage does not ____ from plant to plant over time.
e: Abiotic damage does not spread from plant to plant over time. Write spread in the gap.

q: Abiotic diseases do not show the presence of disease ____.
e: Abiotic diseases do not show the presence of disease signs. That missing piece is signs.

q: Plant diseases occurrence and severity result from the impact of three factors: the host plant, the pathogen and the ____ conditions.
e: Plant diseases occurrence and severity result from the impact of three factors: the host plant, the pathogen and the environmental conditions. Write environmental in the gap.

q: Signs of plant disease are physical ____ of the pathogen.
e: Signs of plant disease are physical evidence of the pathogen. The blank is evidence.

q: Signs can also help with plant disease ____.
e: Signs can also help with plant disease identification. That missing piece is identification.

q: Signs are the actual ____ causing the disease.
e: Signs are the actual organisms causing the disease. That missing piece is organisms.

q: Signs include conks, fruiting bodies, mildew, mushrooms, mycelium, rhizomorphs, slime flux or ooze, spore masses, insects and/or their ____.
e: Signs include conks, fruiting bodies, mildew, mushrooms, mycelium, rhizomorphs, slime flux or ooze, spore masses, insects and/or their frass. The blank is frass.

q: ____ are visible effects of disease on plants.
e: Symptoms are visible effects of disease on plants. Write Symptoms in the gap.

q: Any detectable changes in colour, shape, and/or functions of the plant in response to a pathogen or disease-causing agent is a ____.
e: Any detectable changes in colour, shape, and/or functions of the plant in response to a pathogen or disease-causing agent is a symptom. The blank is symptom.

q: Symptoms of disease are the plant's ____ to the causal agent.
e: Symptoms of disease are the plant's reaction to the causal agent. Write reaction in the gap.

q: Plant symptoms include blight, canker, chlorosis, decline, dieback, distortion, gall or gall-like, gummosis, leaf distortion, leaf scorch, leaf spot, mosaic, necrosis, stunting, wilt, witches' broom, insect feeding ____.
e: Plant symptoms include blight, canker, chlorosis, decline, dieback, distortion, gall or gall-like, gummosis, leaf distortion, leaf scorch, leaf spot, mosaic, necrosis, stunting, wilt, witches' broom, insect feeding injury. The blank is injury.

q: Viruses cause mottling, spots, mosaic-like patterns, crinkling, and other malformations on leaves and ____.
e: Viruses cause mottling, spots, mosaic-like patterns, crinkling, and other malformations on leaves and fruits. That missing piece is fruits.

q: Because viruses are ____, infected plants must be rogued or discarded.
e: Because viruses are systemic, infected plants must be rogued or discarded. That missing piece is systemic.

q: Common virus diseases in plants include curly top virus in tomatoes, cucumber ____ virus in tomatoes and vine crops.
e: Common virus diseases in plants include curly top virus in tomatoes, cucumber mosaic virus in tomatoes and vine crops. That missing piece is mosaic.

q: Fungi and fungal-like organisms (FLOs) cause more plant diseases than any other group of plant pest with over ____ species shown to cause disease.
e: Fungi and fungal-like organisms (FLOs) cause more plant diseases than any other group of plant pest with over 8,000 species shown to cause disease. That missing piece is 8,000.

q: FLOs are organisms like Pythium and Phytophthora and cause downy ____.
e: FLOs are organisms like Pythium and Phytophthora and cause downy mildew. Write mildew in the gap.

q: Most pathogenic fungi belong to the following genera: Alternaria, Aspergillus, Botrytis, Fusarium, Puccinia, Rhizopus, and ____.
e: Most pathogenic fungi belong to the following genera: Alternaria, Aspergillus, Botrytis, Fusarium, Puccinia, Rhizopus, and sclerotinia. That missing piece is sclerotinia.

q: Alternaria causes leaf spots and ____ of various plants.
e: Alternaria causes leaf spots and blight of various plants. The blank is blight.

q: Aspergillus causes rots of ____.
e: Aspergillus causes rots of seeds. Write seeds in the gap.

q: Puccinia causes ____ of cereals.
e: Puccinia causes rust of cereals. The blank is rust.

q: Rhizopus causes soft rot of ____.
e: Rhizopus causes soft rot of fruits. Write fruits in the gap.

q: Sclerotinia causes soft rot of ____.
e: Sclerotinia causes soft rot of vegetables. Write vegetables in the gap.

q: Not all bacteria are bad for plants and soil; in fact, most are ____.
e: Not all bacteria are bad for plants and soil; in fact, most are beneficial. That missing piece is beneficial.

q: There are approximately ____ types of bacteria that cause diseases in plants.
e: There are approximately 200 types of bacteria that cause diseases in plants. The blank is 200.

q: Bacteria that cause plant diseases are most active in warm and ____ environments.
e: Bacteria that cause plant diseases are most active in warm and humid environments. The blank is humid.

q: Most plant pathogenic bacteria belong to the following genera: Agrobacterium, Erwinia, Pseudomonas, Streptomyces and ____.
e: Most plant pathogenic bacteria belong to the following genera: Agrobacterium, Erwinia, Pseudomonas, Streptomyces and xanthomonas. The blank is xanthomonas.

q: Nematodes are simple, multicellular animals and are bilaterally symmetrical, soft-bodied, non-segmented ____.
e: Nematodes are simple, multicellular animals and are bilaterally symmetrical, soft-bodied, non-segmented roundworms. The blank is roundworms.

q: Most nematode species that attack plants are ____.
e: Most nematode species that attack plants are microscopic. The blank is microscopic.

q: Plant parasitic nematodes have a ____, a piercing mouthpart.
e: Plant parasitic nematodes have a stylet, a piercing mouthpart. The blank is stylet.

q: The presence of a stylet is the key diagnostic sign differentiating plant parasitic nematodes from all other types of ____.
e: The presence of a stylet is the key diagnostic sign differentiating plant parasitic nematodes from all other types of nematodes. That missing piece is nematodes.

q: Root-knot nematodes belong to the genus ____.
e: Root-knot nematodes belong to the genus meloidogyne. Write meloidogyne in the gap.

q: Plant diseases caused by infectious pathogens have seriously affected human society and nature through their damages to food production, ____ development.
e: Plant diseases caused by infectious pathogens have seriously affected human society and nature through their damages to food production, economic development. That missing piece is economic.

q: To prevent, mitigate or control plant diseases, different approaches can be used: biological, physical and ____.
e: To prevent, mitigate or control plant diseases, different approaches can be used: biological, physical and chemical. The blank is chemical.

q: Biological control is control of plant diseases using living ____.
e: Biological control is control of plant diseases using living microorganisms. Write microorganisms in the gap.

q: Physical methods of disease prevention are based on the physiological ____ of disease agents to adverse conditions.
e: Physical methods of disease prevention are based on the physiological tolerance of disease agents to adverse conditions. That missing piece is tolerance.

q: Physical control involves the removal of pathogen sources or presence of physical ____ to prevent contact between the disease agent and the host.
e: Physical control involves the removal of pathogen sources or presence of physical barriers to prevent contact between the disease agent and the host. That missing piece is barriers.

q: Chemicals used to control bacteria (____), fungi (fungicides), and nematodes (nematicides) may be applied to seeds, foliage, flowers, fruit, or soil.
e: Chemicals used to control bacteria (bactericides), fungi (fungicides), and nematodes (nematicides) may be applied to seeds, foliage, flowers, fruit, or soil. That missing piece is bactericides.

q: Chemicals used to control fungi are known as ____.
e: Chemicals used to control fungi are known as fungicides. The blank is fungicides.

q: Chemicals used to control nematodes are known as ____.
e: Chemicals used to control nematodes are known as nematicides. The blank is nematicides.

q: A disease is an illness or disorder of the body or mind that leads to poor ____.
e: A disease is an illness or disorder of the body or mind that leads to poor health. The blank is health.

q: All animals, including human, suffer from one kind of disease or another during their ____.
e: All animals, including human, suffer from one kind of disease or another during their lifespan. That missing piece is lifespan.

q: Animal diseases can be divided into non-infectious diseases and ____ diseases.
e: Animal diseases can be divided into non-infectious diseases and infectious diseases. The blank is infectious.

q: Non-infectious diseases are those that are not caused by ____, so that they cannot spread from one person to another.
e: Non-infectious diseases are those that are not caused by pathogens, so that they cannot spread from one person to another. Write pathogens in the gap.

q: Non-infectious diseases are caused by factors such as aging, genetics, malnutrition, lifestyle and ____.
e: Non-infectious diseases are caused by factors such as aging, genetics, malnutrition, lifestyle and environment. Write environment in the gap.

q: Examples of non-infectious diseases include cardiovascular disease, cancer, chronic respiratory disease, diabetes, and ____.
e: Examples of non-infectious diseases include cardiovascular disease, cancer, chronic respiratory disease, diabetes, and alzheimer's. That missing piece is alzheimer's.

q: Most cardiovascular disease starts with ____ formation.
e: Most cardiovascular disease starts with atheroma formation. Write atheroma in the gap.

q: If the ____, the inner lining of the wall of the artery, is damaged by high blood pressure, an inflammatory response where by white blood cells (mostly macrophages) move into the area.
e: If the endothelium, the inner lining of the wall of the artery, is damaged by high blood pressure, an inflammatory response where by white blood cells (mostly macrophages) move into the area. The blank is endothelium.

q: White blood cells (mostly macrophages) and lipids from the blood clump together under the endothelium to form fatty ____.
e: White blood cells (mostly macrophages) and lipids from the blood clump together under the endothelium to form fatty streaks. That missing piece is streaks.

q: Over time, more white blood cells, lipids and connective tissue build up and harden to form a fibrous plaque called ____.
e: Over time, more white blood cells, lipids and connective tissue build up and harden to form a fibrous plaque called atheroma. Write atheroma in the gap.

q: The hardening of arteries, caused by atheroma, is called ____.
e: The hardening of arteries, caused by atheroma, is called atherosclerosis. The blank is atherosclerosis.

q: In angina, plaques build up slowly in the ____ arteries, reducing blood flow to the parts of the heart muscle.
e: In angina, plaques build up slowly in the coronary arteries, reducing blood flow to the parts of the heart muscle. The blank is coronary.

q: Often symptoms of angina are first noticed during ____, when the cardiac muscle is working harder and needs more oxygen.
e: Often symptoms of angina are first noticed during exercise, when the cardiac muscle is working harder and needs more oxygen. Write exercise in the gap.

q: The narrowed coronary arteries cannot supply enough oxygenated blood and the heart muscle resorts to ____ respiration.
e: The narrowed coronary arteries cannot supply enough oxygenated blood and the heart muscle resorts to anaerobic respiration. That missing piece is anaerobic.

q: The symptoms of angina subside once exercise ____.
e: The symptoms of angina subside once exercise stops. That missing piece is stops.

q: Oxygen is supplied to the heart muscle by the ____ arteries.
e: Oxygen is supplied to the heart muscle by the coronary arteries. The blank is coronary.

q: If the coronary artery becomes completely blocked by a blood clot, an area of the heart muscle will be totally cut off from its blood supply, causing myocardial ____.
e: If the coronary artery becomes completely blocked by a blood clot, an area of the heart muscle will be totally cut off from its blood supply, causing myocardial infarction. The blank is infarction.

q: Myocardial infarction is more commonly known as a heart ____.
e: Myocardial infarction is more commonly known as a heart attack. Write attack in the gap.

q: A stroke is caused by an interruption to the normal blood supply to an area of the ____.
e: A stroke is caused by an interruption to the normal blood supply to an area of the brain. The blank is brain.

q: A blockage in the brain is usually caused by a blood clot, an atheroma or a combination of the ____.
e: A blockage in the brain is usually caused by a blood clot, an atheroma or a combination of the two. Write two in the gap.

q: Very often in a stroke, the blood is cut off from one part or one ____ of the brain only.
e: Very often in a stroke, the blood is cut off from one part or one side of the brain only. Write side in the gap.

q: In more severe strokes, there can be ____, usually on one side of the body.
e: In more severe strokes, there can be paralysis, usually on one side of the body. Write paralysis in the gap.

q: Deep vein thrombosis (DVT) is the formation of a blood clot in a vein ____ inside the body.
e: Deep vein thrombosis (DVT) is the formation of a blood clot in a vein deep inside the body. The blank is deep.

q: Deep vein thrombosis (DVT) usually happens in ____ veins.
e: Deep vein thrombosis (DVT) usually happens in leg veins. That missing piece is leg.

q: DVT can be caused by prolong inactivity such as during long-haul ____.
e: DVT can be caused by prolong inactivity such as during long-haul flights. Write flights in the gap.

q: The three main risk factors for CVDs which cannot be changed are genes, age, and ____.
e: The three main risk factors for CVDs which cannot be changed are genes, age, and gender. Write gender in the gap.

q: As a person gets older, the blood vessels begin to lose their ____ and to narrow slightly.
e: As a person gets older, the blood vessels begin to lose their elasticity and to narrow slightly. The blank is elasticity.

q: Men are more likely to suffer from heart disease (and other CVDs) than ____.
e: Men are more likely to suffer from heart disease (and other CVDs) than women. The blank is women.

q: Substances in tobacco smoke can damage the artery ____, which makes the build-up of plaques more likely.
e: Substances in tobacco smoke can damage the artery linings, which makes the build-up of plaques more likely. That missing piece is linings.

q: Smoking also changes the balance of ____ in the blood.
e: Smoking also changes the balance of lipoproteins in the blood. The blank is lipoproteins.

q: Sedentary lifestyle can lead to heart diseases, obesity, high blood pressure and ____.
e: Sedentary lifestyle can lead to heart diseases, obesity, high blood pressure and diabetes. Write diabetes in the gap.

q: A healthy blood pressure is around ____ mmHg during systole and around80 mmHg during diastole.
e: A healthy blood pressure is around 120 mmHg during systole and around80 mmHg during diastole. The blank is 120.

q: If the blood pressure is regularly above 140/90 mmHg, it is a sign of high blood pressure or ____.
e: If the blood pressure is regularly above 140/90 mmHg, it is a sign of high blood pressure or hypertension. That missing piece is hypertension.

q: Most scientists think that the best predictors of future CVDs are where fat is stored on the body, how much exercise a person does and the levels of different ____ in the blood.
e: Most scientists think that the best predictors of future CVDs are where fat is stored on the body, how much exercise a person does and the levels of different fats in the blood. The blank is fats.

q: Type 2 diabetes can result in damage to the lining of the blood vessels which increases the risk of ____ formation.
e: Type 2 diabetes can result in damage to the lining of the blood vessels which increases the risk of plaque formation. The blank is plaque.

q: Eating a balanced diet with a variety of fats and plenty of fruit and ____ helps prevent atherosclerosis.
e: Eating a balanced diet with a variety of fats and plenty of fruit and vegetables helps prevent atherosclerosis. Write vegetables in the gap.

q: Not smoking and maintaining a healthy ____- a body mass index (BMI) of 18.5- 25 kgm is the ideal range.
e: Not smoking and maintaining a healthy weight- a body mass index (BMI) of 18.5- 25 kgm is the ideal range. Write weight in the gap.

q: Taking regular exercise strengthens the heart muscle and helps to control blood pressure and ____ level.
e: Taking regular exercise strengthens the heart muscle and helps to control blood pressure and cholesterol level. Write cholesterol in the gap.

q: Antihypertensives drugs such as beta blockers, sympathetic nerve inhibitors, ACE inhibitors are prescribed to reduce blood ____.
e: Antihypertensives drugs such as beta blockers, sympathetic nerve inhibitors, ACE inhibitors are prescribed to reduce blood pressure. Write pressure in the gap.

q: To lower the level of cholesterol in the blood, a group of drugs known as ____ is used.
e: To lower the level of cholesterol in the blood, a group of drugs known as statin is used. Write statin in the gap.

q: Statins improve the balance of LDLs (low-density lipoprotein) to ____ (high-density lipoprotein).
e: Statins improve the balance of LDLs (low-density lipoprotein) to HDLs (high-density lipoprotein). The blank is HDLs.

q: Plant stanols and sterols compounds are now widely sold in spreads and ____, which also reduce the levels of LDLs in the blood.
e: Plant stanols and sterols compounds are now widely sold in spreads and yoghurts, which also reduce the levels of LDLs in the blood. Write yoghurts in the gap.

q: Anticoagulants (e.g., warfarin and heparin) are a class of medicines used to reduce blood ____.
e: Anticoagulants (e.g., warfarin and heparin) are a class of medicines used to reduce blood clotting. That missing piece is clotting.

q: Platelet inhibitory drugs such as ____ are also a type of anticoagulant.
e: Platelet inhibitory drugs such as aspirin are also a type of anticoagulant. Write aspirin in the gap.

q: Infectious diseases are diseases that are caused by organisms known as ____.
e: Infectious diseases are diseases that are caused by organisms known as pathogens. Write pathogens in the gap.

q: Infectious diseases are sometimes called ____ diseases as they are passed from infected to uninfected people.
e: Infectious diseases are sometimes called communicable diseases as they are passed from infected to uninfected people. Write communicable in the gap.

q: The way in which a pathogen passes from one host to another is called the transmission ____.
e: The way in which a pathogen passes from one host to another is called the transmission cycle. The blank is cycle.

q: The ____ of a disease is the number of people who have that disease at any one time.
e: The prevalence of a disease is the number of people who have that disease at any one time. That missing piece is prevalence.

q: Diseases that are always in populations are described as ____.
e: Diseases that are always in populations are described as endemic. The blank is endemic.

q: An ____ occurs when there is a sudden increase in the number of people with a disease.
e: An epidemic occurs when there is a sudden increase in the number of people with a disease. That missing piece is epidemic.

q: A ____ occurs when there is an increase in the number of cases throughout a continent or across the world.
e: A pandemic occurs when there is an increase in the number of cases throughout a continent or across the world. Write pandemic in the gap.

q: The death rate from different diseases is referred to as ____.
e: The death rate from different diseases is referred to as mortality. The blank is mortality.

q: Cholera is caused by the bacterium Vibrio ____.
e: Cholera is caused by the bacterium Vibrio cholerae. The blank is cholerae.

q: Malaria is caused by four species of ____.
e: Malaria is caused by four species of plasmodium. The blank is plasmodium.

q: HIV/AIDS is caused by the Human Immunodeficiency Virus, which is a type of ____.
e: HIV/AIDS is caused by the Human Immunodeficiency Virus, which is a type of virus. The blank is virus.

q: Tuberculosis (TB) is caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis and M. ____.
e: Tuberculosis (TB) is caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis and M. bovis. The blank is bovis.

q: Most cases of malaria are caused by one of four species of the protist ____.
e: Most cases of malaria are caused by one of four species of the protist plasmodium. The blank is plasmodium.

q: The method of transmission for malaria is an insect vector: the female ____ mosquito.
e: The method of transmission for malaria is an insect vector: the female anopheles mosquito. That missing piece is anopheles.

q: Malaria is endemic in ____ countries globally.
e: Malaria is endemic in 106 countries globally. That missing piece is 106.

q: The incubation period for malaria is from a week to a ____.
e: The incubation period for malaria is from a week to a year. That missing piece is year.

q: The site of action of the malaria pathogen includes the liver, red blood cells, and ____.
e: The site of action of the malaria pathogen includes the liver, red blood cells, and brain. The blank is brain.

q: Clinical features of malaria include fever, anaemia, nausea, headaches, muscle pain, shivering, sweating, and enlarged ____.
e: Clinical features of malaria include fever, anaemia, nausea, headaches, muscle pain, shivering, sweating, and enlarged spleen. Write spleen in the gap.

q: Malaria can be diagnosed by microscopical examination of blood or a dip stick test for malaria ____ in blood.
e: Malaria can be diagnosed by microscopical examination of blood or a dip stick test for malaria antigens in blood. That missing piece is antigens.

q: In 2012, there were about 207 million cases of malaria worldwide, with about 80% in ____.
e: In 2012, there were about 207 million cases of malaria worldwide, with about 80% in africa. That missing piece is africa.

q: Female Anopheles mosquitoes feed on human blood to obtain the ____ they need to develop their eggs.
e: Female Anopheles mosquitoes feed on human blood to obtain the protein they need to develop their eggs. That missing piece is protein.

q: Male and female gametes fuse in the mosquito's ____ and develop to form infective stages.
e: Male and female gametes fuse in the mosquito's gut and develop to form infective stages. That missing piece is gut.

q: When the mosquito feeds again, it injects an ____ from its salivary glands that prevents the blood meal from clotting.
e: When the mosquito feeds again, it injects an anticoagulant from its salivary glands that prevents the blood meal from clotting. That missing piece is anticoagulant.

q: The parasites enter the red blood cells, where they ____.
e: The parasites enter the red blood cells, where they multiply. The blank is multiply.

q: Malaria may also be transmitted during blood ____ and when unsterile needles are re-used.
e: Malaria may also be transmitted during blood transfusion and when unsterile needles are re-used. That missing piece is transfusion.

q: Plasmodium can also pass across the ____ from mother to fetus.
e: Plasmodium can also pass across the placenta from mother to fetus. That missing piece is placenta.

q: If people are continually re-infected by different strains of malaria they become ____.
e: If people are continually re-infected by different strains of malaria they become immune. Write immune in the gap.

q: Immunity to malaria only lasts as long as people are in ____ with the disease.
e: Immunity to malaria only lasts as long as people are in contact with the disease. That missing piece is contact.

q: Quinine and chloroquine are anti-malarial drugs used to treat infected people and as ____ drugs.
e: Quinine and chloroquine are anti-malarial drugs used to treat infected people and as prophylactic drugs. The blank is prophylactic.

q: Chloroquine inhibits protein synthesis and prevents the parasite ____ within the body.
e: Chloroquine inhibits protein synthesis and prevents the parasite spreading within the body. That missing piece is spreading.

q: Proguanil has the added advantage of inhibiting the sexual ____ of Plasmodium inside the biting mosquito.
e: Proguanil has the added advantage of inhibiting the sexual reproduction of Plasmodium inside the biting mosquito. Write reproduction in the gap.

q: Where anti-malarial drugs have been used widely, there are strains of drug-resistant ____.
e: Where anti-malarial drugs have been used widely, there are strains of drug-resistant plasmodium. The blank is plasmodium.

q: Mefloquine is a new drug used in South America, Africa and New ____.
e: Mefloquine is a new drug used in South America, Africa and New guinea. Write guinea in the gap.

q: Artesunate, a drug derived from the plant compound ____, is used in combination with mefloquine to treat infections of P. falciparum.
e: Artesunate, a drug derived from the plant compound artemisinin, is used in combination with mefloquine to treat infections of P. falciparum. The blank is artemisinin.

q: There are three main ways to control malaria: reduce the number of mosquitoes, avoid being bitten, and use ____ to prevent the parasite infecting people.
e: There are three main ways to control malaria: reduce the number of mosquitoes, avoid being bitten, and use drugs to prevent the parasite infecting people. That missing piece is drugs.

q: Mosquitoes lay their eggs in ____.
e: Mosquitoes lay their eggs in water. Write water in the gap.

q: Oil can be spread over the surfaces of water to make it impossible for mosquito larvae and pupae to ____.
e: Oil can be spread over the surfaces of water to make it impossible for mosquito larvae and pupae to breathe. That missing piece is breathe.

q: Stocking ponds with fish which feed on mosquito larvae, e.g., mosquito fish Gambusia ____.
e: Stocking ponds with fish which feed on mosquito larvae,, mosquito fish Gambusia affinis. Write affinis in the gap.

q: Spraying a preparation containing the bacterium Bacillus ____, which kills mosquito larvae but is not toxic to other forms of life.
e: Spraying a preparation containing the bacterium Bacillus thuringiensis, which kills mosquito larvae but is not toxic to other forms of life. That missing piece is thuringiensis.

q: The best protection against malaria is to avoid being ____.
e: The best protection against malaria is to avoid being bitten. Write bitten in the gap.

q: People are advised to sleep beneath mosquito ____ and use insect repellents.
e: People are advised to sleep beneath mosquito nets and use insect repellents. Write nets in the gap.

q: Soaking mosquito nets in insecticide every ____ months has been shown to reduce mortality from malaria.
e: Soaking mosquito nets in insecticide every six months has been shown to reduce mortality from malaria. Write six in the gap.

q: In the 1950s, the World Health Organization (WHO) coordinated a worldwide ____ programme.
e: In the 1950s, the World Health Organization (WHO) coordinated a worldwide eradication programme. That missing piece is eradication.

q: The WHO eradication programme was not generally successful because Plasmodium became resistant to the ____ used to control it.
e: The WHO eradication programme was not generally successful because Plasmodium became resistant to the drugs used to control it. That missing piece is drugs.

q: Mosquitoes became resistant to dichloro-diphenyl-trichloroethane (____) and the other insecticides that were used at the time.
e: Mosquitoes became resistant to dichloro-diphenyl-trichloroethane (DDT) and the other insecticides that were used at the time. The blank is DDT.

q: Between 2000 and 2011, control measures achieved a decrease in mortality rates of about 25% across the world, and 33% in the WHO's ____ region.
e: Between 2000 and 2011, control measures achieved a decrease in mortality rates of about 25% across the world, and 33% in the WHO's african region. Write african in the gap.

q: The introduction of simple dip stick tests for diagnosing malaria means that diagnosis can be done quickly without the need for ____.
e: The introduction of simple dip stick tests for diagnosing malaria means that diagnosis can be done quickly without the need for laboratories. Write laboratories in the gap.

q: The whole genome of Plasmodium has been ____, and this may lead to the development of effective vaccines.
e: The whole genome of Plasmodium has been sequenced, and this may lead to the development of effective vaccines. That missing piece is sequenced.

q: Drugs are used in ____ to reduce the chances of drug resistance arising.
e: Drugs are used in combination to reduce the chances of drug resistance arising. Write combination in the gap.
